region.text: Kütahya and its country, with Philadelphia

ledger.note: 1300: Yakub I founds the Germiyan beylik at Kütahya. Infobox 'Established: 1300'; Yakub I's reign is given as 1300-1340 and the dynasty 'controlled parts of western Anatolia from c. 1300 to 1429'. The page names Kütahya (capital), Simav, Kula, Philadelphia, Denizli and Karahisar without dates; the region is Cliopatria's 1305 shape plus Philadelphia.

1304 (spring): the Catalan Company takes Philadelphia. 'Philadelphia (later known as Alaşehir), which he had earlier taken over, was lost to the Catalans' in the spring of 1304. The page also says Simav and Kula 'were later regained by the Catalan Company' (undated).

region.text: the Eğirdir-Isparta lands of the Hamidid shape

ledger.note: 1333: Germiyan takes land round Eğirdir and Isparta from Hamid. The year and the land are Cliopatria's (42 cells of Hamid's last-but-one shape pass to Germiyan); the Germiyanids page is silent on Hamid and the Hamidids page does not mention Germiyan, so this is a bridging entry.

region.text: the rest of the Hamidid shape, with Denizli and Afyon

ledger.note: 1344: Germiyan takes the remaining Hamid lands in Cliopatria (69 of 70 gained western cells lie in Hamid's last shape). The Germiyanids page places 'Denizli and Karahisar' in Yakub I's domain (to 1340) without a date, and the Hamidids page says only that Hamid was 'annexed by the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I in 1391'. Year and land are Cliopatria's.

1363: Cliopatria extends Germiyan east to Ankara. The page says only 'At that time, Yakub's realm extended as east as Ankara' (undated); the counterpart is 'nobody' because Cliopatria has no state there (three cells overlap its Ottoman shape of 1362). A bridging entry.

1381: Suleiman Shah gives Kütahya, Simav, Eğrigöz and Tavşanlı to the Ottomans as the dowry of his daughter Devletşah, who marries Bayezid. 'The wedding took place in 1381 in Kütahya, after which Bayezid became the governor of Kütahya, and Suleiman Shah had to retreat to Kula.' The province is a wider reading of the four towns.
1381: the court retreats from Kütahya to Kula. Infobox 'Kula (1381-1399)'.

region.text: what remained of the realm after the 1381 dowry

ledger.note: 1390: Bayezid I takes the whole of Germiyan. 'In 1390, the entire realm of Germiyan came under Ottoman control, with Yakub no longer as its ruler.' Yakub II is a captive until 1402 and sought Timur's protection in 1399.

1402: Timur's victory over the Ottomans restores Germiyan to Yakub II. 'The Ottomans were ultimately defeated, and Timur restored the former Germiyan possessions to Yakub'; the infobox has Kütahya the capital again from 1402 and the Battle of Ankara page dates the battle to 28 July 1402. The Timurid dossier should carry the other side.

1410 (September): war breaks out between Germiyan and Karaman. 'This escalated to a war between the two in September 1410'; the page gives no earlier campaign, and Kütahya is the place that changes hands.
1411: Kütahya falls to Karaman and the fighting ends in a Karaman gain; no treaty is on the page.
1411: Mehmed II of Karaman takes Kütahya. 'In 1411, Kütahya fell to Mehmed II of Karaman (r. 1398–1399, 1402–1420), interrupting Yakub's reign a second time.'

region.text: Kütahya and Yakub's rule in Germiyan

ledger.note: 1414: Mehmed Çelebi reinstates Yakub II. 'Mehmed Chelebi reinstated Yakub's rule in Germiyan in 1414.' The page does not say who held Kütahya in 1412-1413; Karaman, which took it in 1411, is named as the counterpart.

1429 (January): Yakub II dies and Murad II annexes Germiyan by his will. 'Yakub lacked male heirs and left the sultanate to Murad II in his will shortly before he died in 1429'; 'Murad annexed Germiyan as requested by Yakub, which brought its history to an end'; 'dying in January 1429'.
1429: the Germiyan beylik ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1429'. The Kütahya article gives 1428 for the Ottoman conquest of the city; the Germiyanids page gives January 1429 for Yakub II's death.

wars.outcome: Philadelphia was lost to the Catalans in the spring of 1304; the page adds that Simav and Kula were 'later regained by the Catalan Company' and that Mehmed Chakhshadan 'retook Kula and Angir from the Catalan Company'.

wars.name: Ottoman absorption of Germiyan

zones.text: Kütahya, Simav, Eğrigöz and Tavşanlı, given as a dowry in 1381

wars.note: A diplomatic and then military absorption under Murad I and Bayezid I; the page describes no battle. Listed so that the reviewer sees it was considered.

wars.name: Germiyan-Karaman war of 1410
wars.outcome: Karaman took Kütahya in 1411 and interrupted Yakub's reign; Mehmed Çelebi reinstated Yakub in 1414.

notes: Cliopatria's Germiyanids row is wrong in two ways. (1) From 1344 to 1414 the polygon is a composite: a western Anatolian part of 47.5-52.9 thousand km2 plus an eastern lobe of 38-165 thousand km2 east of 38 E (Diyarbakır, Mardin, Şanlıurfa, Van, Bitlis, Hakkari, Hasakah, Raqqa, Dihok) that no Germiyan page supports and that overlaps no other Cliopatria shape; it looks like another state's territory (Artuqid or Kurdish lands, which Cliopatria lacks) attached to the row. The keyframes cut it away with a western polygon (27-35 E, 35-43 N); a gap-filler or the Jazira agent should find whose land the lobe is. (2) The 1431-1439 remnant at Ankara outlives the dynasty by ten years. Cliopatria also ignores the 1381 dowry, the 1390-1402 Ottoman interval, the 1411-1414 Karaman interruption and ends the row in 1439 instead of January 1429. The Germiyanids page gives no area, so no ratio could be computed; the 1333 and 1344 gains from Hamid and the 1363 Ankara gain rest on Cliopatria shapes only (confidence 1). Pages opened: Germiyanids, Kütahya, Hamidids, Anatolian beyliks, Battle of Ankara; the page budget was five. Not settled: whether Germiyan was an Ilkhanate vassal in 1333-1343 (Cliopatria lists the Ilkhanate as a neighbour; the page says only that Anatolia 'came under the influence of the Ilkhanate'); who held Kütahya in 1412-1413; the Ankara reach (undated). For mirrors: the Ottoman dossier (me-10) should carry gains in 1381, 1390 and 1429 and a loss in 1402; the Karaman dossier a gain of Kütahya in 1411 and a loss in 1414; the Hamid dossier losses in 1333 and 1344; the Timurid dossier the 1402 restoration. Gazetteer: places Alaşehir, Kula, Simav, Tavşanlı, Eğrigöz are missing (only Alaşehir is used as a region; the others are in capitals or text).
